sourceHtml:
Industrial operations present AI challenges that don’t show up in typical enterprise software. In most facilities, plant data and control logic are spread across separate systems from different vendors: programmable logic controllers (PLCs) and distributed control systems (DCS) run the equipment logic, historians record time-series tags under site-specific naming schemes, supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems drive operator screens, and standalone optimization tools or alarm loggers sit on the side. Bolting an external AI agent onto that stack rarely works well in practice. Each system uses its own naming conventions. The logic that actually governs how equipment behaves (the control sequences, state machines, and safety interlocks) is locked inside proprietary controller code that an external tool can’t inspect. Giving a bolt-on agent access across multiple operational technology (OT) systems also means distributing credentials across the plant network.

CrossnoKaye took a different approach to bring physical AI to heavy industry using Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. Its software-defined automation platform, ATLAS, connects live plant data and AI reasoning to closed-loop control of the equipment running food and beverage plants, industrial refrigeration facilities, aggregates quarries, and manufacturing sites. Across more than 100 industrial facilities and 13,000 controlled assets, CrossnoKaye stores over 22 trillion machine data points, ingests more than 50 billion new readings every day, and runs over 1,000 live advanced process control (APC) applications; CrossnoKaye reports that these applications improve production throughput by 11–17 percent while reducing total facility energy costs by an average of 21 percent. Because ATLAS already manages the facility model, the base control software, the historian, and the optimization applications in one platform on AWS, CrossnoKaye’s agentic intelligence system, AURA, has native access to the full operational state of the plant within a single security boundary.

Having the plant context is only half the problem, though. Large language models (LLMs) are good at interpreting engineering context and planning an investigation, but they cannot reliably compute statistics or physical balances over millions of sensor readings in a prompt. To back every numerical answer with real math, AURA uses the code interpreter capability in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore to write and run Python workloads at runtime inside isolated, AWS managed microVM sandboxes, alongside Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and local edge safety controls. This post covers how CrossnoKaye architected ATLAS and AURA on AWS, how AURA uses Amazon Bedrock AgentCore across interactive Chats, repeatable Tasks, and automated Routines, and what the team learned running physical AI in production.

Solution overview

ATLAS controls industrial processes across existing PLC and DCS infrastructure, from kilns, crushers, drying rooms, ovens, and spiral freezers to chillers, turbines, valves, and compressors, without requiring customers to rip and replace plant hardware. Figure 1 illustrates how on-premises ATLAS edge clusters, continuous cloud optimization, and AURA work together on AWS.

Figure 1: CrossnoKaye AURA and ATLAS physical AI architecture with Amazon Bedrock AgentCore

ATLAS and AURA are built around three core layers:

First, the plant is defined in software from the edge up. At each facility, an on-premises ATLAS control panel with redundant computers, power supplies, and network switches (so local control continues uninterrupted while a failed hardware component is replaced) runs a local Kubernetes cluster that uses contract-first microservices, extending the ATLAS cloud platform on AWS to the plant floor. In the cloud, ATLAS authors, validates, and versions the facility’s base control narratives (defining equipment state machines, sequences, operating bounds, interlocks, and alarm rules), which are downloaded to the edge appliances and run locally against existing equipment and controllers. CrossnoKaye reports over 9,000 control software deployments per year and more than 1 million run hours with zero safety incidents. Each edge appliance also acts as an outbound-only information technology/operational technology (IT/OT) gateway that opens zero inbound firewall ports inside the plant, streaming high-frequency telemetry to AWS through Amazon VPC Lattice and Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK). If cloud connectivity drops, the plant continues running safely on the base control narratives on the local edge cluster.

Second, derived engineering signals and closed-loop optimization applications run on top of base control using the same shared plant model. In the cloud, CrossnoKaye’s Scheduling system runs two continuous pipelines from versioned Python packages in Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3), operating on configurable per-instance cadences and event-driven triggers when plant settings change. Synthetic reading algorithms compute derived engineering metrics, such as heat-flow distributions, asset health indices, energy intensity, and mass-balance deviations, and write them back to the historian alongside physical I/O. Closed-loop optimization applications run on top of the base control layer, combining those derived synthetic readings with physics models, model predictive control (MPC), reinforcement learning, utility tariffs, and weather forecasts to compute optimal setpoint schedules. Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues order every schedule and state update by facility before dispatching setpoints to the local base control narrative on the edge cluster, which CrossnoKaye reports runs 650,000 closed-loop control actions per day.

Third, AURA runs inside the platform boundary on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) as microservices and durable Temporal workflows. Under the caller’s enterprise permissions, AURA agents query the internal Atlas Data gateway to read the operational state of a facility or fleet in one consistent model: upstream and downstream equipment topology, the deployed base control narratives and interlocks, physical I/O and synthetic readings, setting change and alarm histories, active optimization schedules, and plant documentation indexed in Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases.

Having the equipment layout, the base control logic, and the sensor data in the same system makes a concrete difference when diagnosing plant issues. At an aggregates quarry running primary, secondary, and tertiary rock crushers, the back half of the plant tripped twice in a single shift. From the control room, operators saw the secondary crusher fault, cleared the alarm, and restarted the line, only for it to trip again hours later. In the historian timestamps alone, the secondary crusher faulted seconds after the tertiary crusher, which made it look like a crusher problem. Because AURA also reads the conveyor layout and the deployed base control interlocks, its investigation followed the actual control logic. A recirculating belt beneath the tertiary crusher was slipping, which tripped the tertiary crusher’s overload interlock. That interlock’s upstream safety interlock immediately halted the secondary crusher to prevent burying a stopped downstream crusher in stone. Instead of chasing a phantom crusher fault, the plant manager sent an operator to inspect the recirculating belt, confirming and fixing the slip in minutes.

The numbered flows in Figure 1 trace how an AURA investigation runs on AWS:

  1. Client and edge ingress: Engineers and Model Context Protocol (MCP) clients connect through AWS WAF and a public Application Load Balancer, where the API gateway validates enterprise single sign-on (SSO) or MCP credentials. Edge telemetry and control schedules flow through Amazon VPC Lattice (authenticated with AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Signature Version 4 (SigV4)) and Amazon MSK.
  2. Context retrieval and guarded inference: AURA workflows read plant state through the Atlas Data gateway and route prompts and organization-scoped Retrieval Augmented Generation (RAG) queries through the Model Gateway to foundation models, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails, and Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases.
  3. Runtime computation dispatch: For statistical, thermodynamic, or multi-dataset math, the workflow streams input datasets over gRPC to AURA’s internal Sandbox Orchestrator service.
  4. Session coordination and live streaming: In interactive sessions, the Sandbox Orchestrator tracks active sandbox session IDs and streams live progress through Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey.
  5. Isolated Python execution: The Sandbox Orchestrator uses the AWS SDK to call the endpoint for the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore runtime, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, staging datasets and running model-authored Python inside an isolated code interpreter microVM.
  6. Artifact storage and Brief delivery: Verified Apache Parquet outputs, charts, and cited Briefs are saved to Amazon S3 over AWS PrivateLink, and Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) delivers automated Briefs to plant teams.

Walkthrough

AURA combines foundation models on Amazon Bedrock (for model availability by AWS Region, refer to Supported models by AWS Region in the Amazon Bedrock User Guide) with isolated Python sandboxes in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, across three operational modes:

  • Chats: Interactive, multi-turn engineering conversations spanning a single unit, a process line, or a multi-site portfolio (up to 200 facilities in a single turn).
  • Tasks: Repeatable, parameterized investigations bound to immutable version snapshots that produce structured technical Briefs with cited evidence tables and charts.
  • Routines: Automated background watchers triggered by schedules, sensor thresholds, rate-of-change windows, alarms, or equipment mode transitions.

The following sections examine four architectural decisions behind these workflows.

Warm conversational sandboxes compared to clean single-run pipelines

Interactive debugging and automated plant reporting have different state requirements:

  • In an interactive Chat, an engineer explores hypotheses step by step: loading 24 hours of critical alarms across 94 facilities, filtering out chattering tank-level sensors at one site, and correlating compressor trips against ambient wet-bulb temperatures. Starting a cold sandbox on every turn would wipe in-memory tables and add latency. For Chats, the Sandbox Orchestrator binds one warm Amazon Bedrock AgentCore session to the conversation in Amazon ElastiCache for Valkey with a 15-minute sliding time to live (TTL), transparently provisioning a replacement session if an engineer returns after the idle timeout expires.
  • In a scheduled Task or a 2:00 AM Routine, reproducibility comes first. Every run must start in a clean environment with no leftover state from prior runs. For Tasks and Routines, the Sandbox Orchestrator provisions a fresh, single-use AgentCore microVM per run and stops the session with StopCodeInterpreterSession as soon as the calculation finishes, preventing both cross-run contamination and idle sandbox charges.

This warm-session design makes fleet-wide triage practical in a single conversation. When an operations director asks AURA to review all critical alarms across 94 facilities over the past 24 hours and identify the primary mechanical risks, the agent loads the fleet alarm summaries from the Atlas Data gateway into its AgentCore sandbox and groups activations by facility, rule, and inter-arrival time. Rather than ranking sites by raw alarm count, the Python analysis separates a plant where 103 critical activations came from two repeating dump-tank level rules from a plant where 58 activations spanned ammonia detection, evaporator faults, and hot-gas valves within one second of each other, pointing safety and maintenance teams directly to the facility with cascading equipment faults.

Verifiable computation instead of unverified model math

When an engineer asks AURA to analyze a process trend or audit shift performance, the numbers in the response must be exact. Early in AURA’s development, the team found that letting a model write free-form Python scripts that print JSON or text summaries to standard output was too brittle: a model would occasionally misname a column, drop part of a time window, or format output in a way that broke downstream chart rendering.

To make runtime computation verifiable, AURA enforces strict data contracts around every Amazon Bedrock AgentCore run:

  1. Upfront contract validation and multi-source staging: Before allocating a sandbox session, the Sandbox Orchestrator validates the input contract and stages up to 50 datasets into the microVM workspace, combining physical I/O, derived synthetic readings, setting logs, alarm histories, and utility rate tables.
  2. In-sandbox DataFrame schema verification: Rather than parsing free-form text from standard output, the service appends a deterministic verification harness to the model’s Python script. Inside the sandbox, the harness verifies that every declared output table exists in memory as a pandas.DataFrame with all required columns and types, and serializes the verified tables directly to binary Apache Parquet files.
  3. Automated self-correction: If the script raises a Python exception or omits a required column, no unverified numbers reach the user. The Temporal workflow captures the traceback and schema mismatch as a structured retry prompt so the agent fixes its Python logic and re-runs the calculation in a clean sandbox before publishing any conclusion.

Automated night-shift Routines and cited Briefs through Amazon SES

Plant engineers cannot watch dashboards across 100 facilities around the clock, and many equipment issues start as slow drift on the night shift. AURA Routines run in the background, watching for specific process conditions (such as suction-pressure drift on a refrigeration stage, a batch drying curve falling behind specification, or an unscheduled manual setpoint override) and launching an investigation automatically when one triggers.

A night-shift catch on an industrial chiller plant shows how this works end to end:

  1. Automated detection and sandboxed root-cause analysis (02:00–02:03 AM): At 2:00 AM, a Routine detects low-stage suction-pressure drift and launches its pinned Task in read-only mode. Inside an Amazon Bedrock AgentCore sandbox, the agent correlates condenser approach temperatures against low-stage suction pressure across physical and synthetic readings, rules out sensor drift and low refrigerant charge, and isolates condenser-side fouling.
  2. Deterministic citation validation (02:04 AM): Before publishing the Brief, AURA parses every inline citation and verifies that each claim links to a saved telemetry window, setting change record, or sandbox output artifact in Amazon S3. No control change is made automatically.
  3. Brief delivery through Amazon SES and one-click Chat handoff: Within four minutes of the trigger, AURA sends a formatted HTML Brief email through Amazon SES to the plant engineering team with the diagnosis, cited signal traces, and an “Investigate in AURA” button. When the lead engineer selects that button before the morning shift huddle, AURA verifies the engineer’s live facility permissions and opens an interactive Chat pre-loaded with the Brief’s evidence so the team can ask follow-up questions or issue a work order immediately.

Defense in depth industrial safety

In an industrial plant, operational safety cannot depend on an LLM following instructions in a prompt. Because ATLAS and AURA share the same platform from the cloud down to the edge Kubernetes cluster on the plant floor, CrossnoKaye enforces strict boundaries on what AI and optimization workloads can do across four independent layers:

  1. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and verifiable provenance (Observe): Every prompt and completion routed through AURA’s Model Gateway is evaluated by Amazon Bedrock Guardrails to enforce content, topic, and safety policies. Knowledge Base retrieval is isolated by organization, and every Brief requires verified inline citations, noting both which time windows were analyzed and any periods where sensor data was unavailable.
  2. Air-gapped read-only sandboxes and human-approved proposals (Propose): Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter microVMs run in isolated, AWS managed environments with no network routes, credentials, or API paths to plant equipment. Automated Routines run strictly in read-only mode. When an engineer uses an interactive session to propose a setting change, the platform requires explicit human approval under the operator’s corporate identity and verifies the physical outcome in plant telemetry afterward.
  3. Non-bypassable deterministic Level 1 base control at the edge (Bounded and Base Control): Cloud optimization applications don’t drive field hardware directly. They run on top of the platform’s base control layer by dispatching setpoint schedules within engineering-approved envelopes. On the plant floor, the edge Kubernetes cluster runs the downloaded base control narratives locally in real time, enforcing deterministic state-machine guards, rate-of-change clamps, operating bounds, and equipment interlocks that cannot be bypassed by cloud services, optimization applications, or AI agents.
  4. Independent physical hardware protection: Beneath the ATLAS software-defined controller, the plant’s physical machinery and field wiring enforce independent, hardwired protection layers, including safety relays, local programmable trips, and mechanical pressure-relief and over-temperature devices.

Results and lessons learned

Across food processing, industrial refrigeration, aggregates and mining, and manufacturing sites, CrossnoKaye reports that combining software-defined edge control, continuous cloud optimization, and AURA has reduced batch drying-time standard deviation by 34 percent (with 6 percent more product finishing within target yield specification) and identified more than 50,000 tons per year of recoverable production gap in quarry operations. With over 5,000 AI agents monitoring more than 10,000 plant assets across customer facilities (including over 13,000 controlled devices and equipment units across the ATLAS fleet), investigations that previously required hours of exporting historian CSVs, cross-referencing PLC ladder logic, and building spreadsheets now complete in under four minutes, delivering cited technical Briefs through Amazon SES before the morning shift meeting.

Three lessons stood out from building and operating AURA across industrial facilities:

  1. Unify the plant model and control logic before adding AI: An agent can only diagnose real physical root causes, like distinguishing a slipping downstream recirculating belt from a secondary crusher fault, when it can read the process topology, the deployed base control narratives and interlocks, the setting change history, and the optimizer state in one consistent model rather than stitching together six disconnected plant systems.
  2. Deliver value inside the operator’s daily workflow, not as a separate tool to go use: Plant teams are busy running equipment. If an AI assistant is a separate destination where engineers must start from a blank prompt, day-to-day adoption stalls. Embedding AURA into the daily shift rhythm (where background Routines catch anomalies overnight, run the Python analysis in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and deliver a cited Brief to the engineer’s inbox with a one-click handoff into a pre-loaded Chat) means operators see the value in their normal routine without having to go use a separate product.
  3. Enforce data, coverage, and safety contracts in code rather than prompts: In a plant, a missing hour of sensor data isn’t the same as an hour with no events, and an unverified calculation can send a maintenance crew to the wrong machine. Making data-coverage gaps explicit in tool contracts, verifying pandas.DataFrame schemas inside the AgentCore sandbox before extracting binary Apache Parquet outputs, and enforcing deterministic base control bounds on the edge Kubernetes cluster catch probabilistic model errors before they reach an operator or a piece of equipment.

Conclusion

Reliable physical AI in heavy industry requires grounding models in the actual equipment topology and control logic of the plant, and backing every quantitative claim with verifiable Python calculations. Together with Amazon Bedrock Guardrails and isolated Python sandboxes in Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, ATLAS and AURA allow agents to reason over live facility ontology, base control narratives, setting histories, physical I/O, optimization state, and synthetic readings, delivering checkable engineering answers and cited technical Briefs through Amazon SES while keeping deterministic safety controls firmly on the plant floor.

To learn more about building agents with isolated code execution, refer to the Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Developer Guide or visit CrossnoKaye to see how physical AI is transforming heavy industry.

About the authors

translation.html:
工业运营给 AI 带来了一些典型企业软件中不会出现的挑战。在大多数工厂中，工厂数据和控制逻辑分散在不同供应商提供的独立系统中：可编程逻辑控制器（PLC）和分布式控制系统（DCS）运行设备逻辑，历史数据库按照各厂特有的命名规则记录时间序列标签，监控与数据采集（SCADA）系统驱动操作员界面，独立的优化工具或报警记录器则在一旁运行。实践中，将外部 AI 智能体外挂到这套技术栈上，通常效果不佳。每个系统都有自己的命名约定。真正决定设备如何运行的逻辑（控制序列、状态机和安全联锁）封闭在专有控制器代码中，外部工具无法检查。让外挂式智能体跨多个运营技术（OT）系统获得访问权限，也意味着要在整个工厂网络中分发凭证。

CrossnoKaye 采用了不同的方法，利用 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 将物理 AI 引入重工业。其软件定义自动化平台 ATLAS 将实时工厂数据和 AI 推理与设备的闭环控制连接起来，这些设备运行于食品饮料工厂、工业制冷设施、骨料采石场和制造工厂。在 100 多座工业设施、13,000 项受控资产中，CrossnoKaye 存储了超过 22 万亿个机器数据点，每天摄取超过 500 亿条新读数，并运行着 1,000 多个在线高级过程控制（APC）应用；CrossnoKaye 表示，这些应用将生产吞吐量提高了 11%–17%，同时将设施的总能源成本平均降低了 21%。由于 ATLAS 已经在 AWS 上的同一个平台中管理设施模型、基础控制软件、历史数据库和优化应用，CrossnoKaye 的智能体智能系统 AURA 能够在单一安全边界内原生访问工厂的完整运行状态。

不过，掌握工厂上下文只解决了一半问题。大语言模型（LLM）擅长解读工程上下文和规划调查，但无法在提示词中可靠地对数百万条传感器读数进行统计计算或物理平衡计算。为了让每个数值答案都有真实数学计算支撑，AURA 使用 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的代码解释器能力，在运行时于 AWS 托管的隔离 microVM 沙箱内编写并执行 Python 工作负载，同时配合 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 和本地边缘安全控制。本文介绍 CrossnoKaye 如何在 AWS 上设计 ATLAS 和 AURA 的架构，AURA 如何在交互式 Chats、可重复执行的 Tasks 和自动化 Routines 中使用 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore，以及团队在生产环境中运行物理 AI 时获得的经验。

解决方案概述

ATLAS 在现有 PLC 和 DCS 基础设施之上控制工业过程，涵盖窑炉、破碎机、干燥室、烤炉、螺旋速冻机，以及冷水机组、涡轮机、阀门和压缩机，无需客户拆除并更换工厂硬件。图 1 展示了本地部署的 ATLAS 边缘集群、持续云端优化和 AURA 如何在 AWS 上协同工作。

图 1：采用 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的 CrossnoKaye AURA 和 ATLAS 物理 AI 架构

ATLAS 和 AURA 围绕三个核心层构建：

第一，从边缘端开始，用软件定义工厂。在每座设施中，本地部署的 ATLAS 控制柜配备冗余计算机、电源和网络交换机（因此在更换故障硬件组件时，本地控制仍能不间断运行），运行着采用契约优先微服务的本地 Kubernetes 集群，将 AWS 上的 ATLAS 云平台延伸至工厂现场。在云端，ATLAS 编写、验证并对设施的基础控制说明进行版本管理（这些说明定义设备状态机、序列、运行边界、联锁和报警规则），随后将其下载到边缘设备，在本地针对现有设备和控制器运行。CrossnoKaye 表示，每年进行超过 9,000 次控制软件部署，累计运行超过 100 万小时，安全事故为零。每台边缘设备还充当仅允许出站连接的信息技术/运营技术（IT/OT）网关，不在工厂内部开放任何入站防火墙端口，并通过 Amazon VPC Lattice 和 Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka（Amazon MSK） 将高频遥测数据流式传输至 AWS。如果云连接中断，工厂仍可依靠本地边缘集群上的基础控制说明安全运行。

第二，派生工程信号和闭环优化应用使用同一个共享工厂模型，在基础控制之上运行。在云端，CrossnoKaye 的 Scheduling 系统使用 Amazon Simple Storage Service（Amazon S3） 中经过版本管理的 Python 包运行两条持续流水线，按照可为每个实例配置的执行周期运行，并在工厂设置发生变化时通过事件触发。合成读数算法计算派生工程指标，例如热流分布、资产健康指数、能源强度和质量平衡偏差，并将它们与物理 I/O 一同写回历史数据库。闭环优化应用运行在基础控制层之上，将这些派生的合成读数与物理模型、模型预测控制（MPC）、强化学习、公用事业费率和天气预报相结合，计算最优设定值计划。Amazon Simple Queue Service（Amazon SQS） FIFO 队列按设施对每项计划和状态更新进行排序，再将设定值下发给边缘集群上的本地基础控制说明；CrossnoKaye 表示，该集群每天执行 650,000 次闭环控制操作。

第三，AURA 在平台边界内的 Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service（Amazon EKS） 上，以微服务和持久化 Temporal 工作流的形式运行。AURA 智能体依据调用者的企业权限，查询内部 Atlas Data 网关，在一个一致的模型中读取单座设施或设施群的运行状态，包括上下游设备拓扑、已部署的基础控制说明和联锁、物理 I/O 与合成读数、设置变更和报警历史、当前生效的优化计划，以及在 Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases 中建立索引的工厂文档。

将设备布局、基础控制逻辑和传感器数据放在同一个系统中，会对工厂问题诊断产生切实影响。在一座运行一级、二级和三级岩石破碎机的骨料采石场，工厂后半段在一个班次内跳停了两次。操作员在控制室看到二级破碎机故障，清除报警并重启生产线，但数小时后生产线再次跳停。仅从历史数据库的时间戳来看，二级破碎机在三级破碎机之后几秒发生故障，让人以为是破碎机本身的问题。由于 AURA 还可以读取输送机布局和已部署的基础控制联锁，其调查沿着实际控制逻辑展开。三级破碎机下方的一条回料输送带发生打滑，触发了三级破碎机的过载联锁。该联锁关联的上游安全联锁随即停止二级破碎机，防止石料掩埋已经停机的下游破碎机。厂长因此没有继续追查并不存在的破碎机故障，而是派操作员检查回料输送带，在几分钟内确认并修复了打滑问题。

图 1 中带编号的流程展示了 AURA 调查如何在 AWS 上运行：

  1. 客户端和边缘入口：工程师及模型上下文协议（MCP）客户端通过 AWS WAF 和公共 Application Load Balancer 连接，由 API 网关验证企业单点登录（SSO）或 MCP 凭证。边缘遥测数据和控制计划通过 Amazon VPC Lattice（使用 AWS Identity and Access Management（IAM）签名版本 4（SigV4）进行身份验证）和 Amazon MSK 传输。
  2. 上下文检索与受防护的推理：AURA 工作流通过 Atlas Data 网关读取工厂状态，并经由 Model Gateway 将提示词和限定于组织范围的检索增强生成（RAG）查询路由至基础模型、Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 和 Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases。
  3. 运行时计算分发：对于统计、热力学或多数据集数学计算，工作流通过 gRPC 将输入数据集流式传输至 AURA 内部的 Sandbox Orchestrator 服务。
  4. 会话协调与实时流式传输：在交互式会话中，Sandbox Orchestrator 跟踪活跃沙箱会话的 ID，并通过适用于 Valkey 的 Amazon ElastiCache 流式传输实时进度。
  5. 隔离的 Python 执行：Sandbox Orchestrator 使用 AWS SDK 调用 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的一项能力——Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 运行时的端点，暂存数据集，并在隔离的代码解释器 microVM 中运行模型编写的 Python 代码。
  6. 产物存储与 Brief 交付：经过验证的 Apache Parquet 输出、图表以及附带引用的 Brief 简报通过 AWS PrivateLink 保存至 Amazon S3，Amazon Simple Email Service（Amazon SES） 则向工厂团队发送自动生成的 Brief。

详细说明

AURA 将 Amazon Bedrock 上的基础模型（有关各 AWS 区域的模型可用性，请参阅《Amazon Bedrock 用户指南》中的各 AWS 区域支持的模型）与 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 的一项能力——Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter 中的隔离 Python 沙箱相结合，支持三种运行模式：

  • Chats：交互式多轮工程对话，可涵盖单个装置、一条工艺生产线或跨多个站点的设施组合（单轮最多涵盖 200 座设施）。
  • Tasks：可重复执行、参数化的调查，绑定不可变的版本快照，生成结构化技术 Brief，其中包含附带引用的证据表格和图表。
  • Routines：自动化后台监测程序，由计划、传感器阈值、变化率窗口、报警或设备模式切换触发。

以下各节将探讨这些工作流背后的四项架构决策。

保持热状态的对话沙箱与干净的单次运行流水线

交互式调试与自动化工厂报告对状态有不同要求：

  • 在交互式 Chat 中，工程师逐步探索假设：加载 94 座设施过去 24 小时的关键报警，筛除其中一座设施中频繁反复报警的罐液位传感器，再将压缩机跳停与环境湿球温度进行关联分析。如果每一轮都冷启动沙箱，就会清空内存中的表并增加延迟。对于 Chats，Sandbox Orchestrator 在适用于 Valkey 的 Amazon ElastiCache 中，将一个保持热状态的 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 会话绑定至对话，并设置 15 分钟的滑动生存时间（TTL）；如果工程师在空闲超时后返回，系统会透明地创建替代会话。
  • 对于定时 Task 或凌晨 2:00 执行的 Routine，可复现性优先。每次运行都必须从干净的环境开始，不保留先前运行的任何状态。对于 Tasks 和 Routines，Sandbox Orchestrator 为每次运行创建全新的、一次性使用的 AgentCore microVM，并在计算完成后立即使用 StopCodeInterpreterSession 停止会话，既防止不同运行之间的状态污染，也避免沙箱空闲产生费用。

这种热会话设计使得在一次对话中对整个设施群进行初步排查成为可能。当运营总监要求 AURA 审查 94 座设施过去 24 小时内的所有关键报警，并识别主要机械风险时，智能体将设施群报警摘要从 Atlas Data 网关加载至其 AgentCore 沙箱，并按设施、规则和相邻触发间隔对报警触发进行分组。Python 分析不会仅按报警总数给设施排序，而是区分出这样的两座工厂：一座工厂的 103 次关键报警触发来自两条反复触发的卸料罐液位规则；另一座工厂的 58 次触发则涉及氨检测、蒸发器故障和热气阀，且彼此间隔不超过一秒。这使安全和维护团队能够直接关注发生级联设备故障的设施。

以可验证的计算取代未经验证的模型数学运算

当工程师要求 AURA 分析工艺趋势或审核班次表现时，回复中的数字必须准确。在 AURA 开发早期，团队发现，让模型自由编写 Python 脚本并将 JSON 或文本摘要打印到标准输出的方式过于脆弱：模型偶尔会写错列名、遗漏部分时间窗口，或采用导致下游图表渲染失败的输出格式。

为了使运行时计算可验证，AURA 对每次 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 运行实施严格的数据契约：

  1. 前置契约验证与多源数据暂存：在分配沙箱会话前，Sandbox Orchestrator 会验证输入契约，并将最多 50 个数据集暂存到 microVM 工作区中，结合物理 I/O、派生合成读数、设置日志、报警历史和公用事业费率表。
  2. 沙箱内的 DataFrame 模式验证：服务不会解析标准输出中的自由格式文本，而是向模型的 Python 脚本追加一套确定性的验证程序。该程序在沙箱内验证每个声明的输出表是否以 pandas.DataFrame 的形式存在于内存中，且包含所有必需的列和类型，然后将验证通过的表直接序列化为二进制 Apache Parquet 文件。
  3. 自动自我纠正：如果脚本引发 Python 异常或缺少必需的列，任何未经验证的数字都不会呈现给用户。Temporal 工作流会捕获异常回溯和模式不匹配信息，将其整理为结构化的重试提示词，让智能体修正其 Python 逻辑，并在干净的沙箱中重新运行计算，然后才发布任何结论。

通过 Amazon SES 提供自动化夜班 Routines 和附带引用的 Brief

工厂工程师无法全天候盯着 100 座设施的仪表盘，而许多设备问题始于夜班期间的缓慢漂移。AURA Routines 在后台运行，监测特定工艺状况（例如某一级制冷的吸气压力漂移、批次干燥曲线落后于规格要求，或计划外的手动设定值覆盖），并在其中某个条件触发时自动启动调查。

一次工业冷水机组工厂的夜班问题发现，展示了这一流程如何端到端运行：

  1. 自动检测与沙箱内根因分析（凌晨 02:00–02:03）：凌晨 2:00，一个 Routine 检测到低压级吸气压力漂移，并以只读模式启动其固定版本的 Task。在 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 沙箱中，智能体结合物理读数和合成读数，对冷凝器接近温差与低压级吸气压力进行关联分析，排除传感器漂移和制冷剂充注不足，最终定位到冷凝器侧结垢。
  2. 确定性的引用验证（凌晨 02:04）：发布 Brief 前，AURA 会解析每一处行内引用，验证每项论断是否链接到 Amazon S3 中保存的遥测时间窗口、设置变更记录或沙箱输出产物。系统不会自动进行任何控制变更。
  3. 通过 Amazon SES 交付 Brief，并一键转入 Chat：触发后四分钟内，AURA 通过 Amazon SES 向工厂工程团队发送排版好的 HTML 格式 Brief 邮件，其中包含诊断结果、附有引用的信号曲线，以及“在 AURA 中调查”按钮。当首席工程师在早班碰头会前选择该按钮时，AURA 会验证工程师当前的设施访问权限，并打开已预载 Brief 证据的交互式 Chat，让团队能够立即追问或下达工单。

工业安全的纵深防御

在工业工厂中，运行安全不能依赖 LLM 遵循提示词中的指令。由于 ATLAS 和 AURA 从云端到工厂现场的边缘 Kubernetes 集群共享同一个平台，CrossnoKaye 通过四个独立层，对 AI 和优化工作负载能够执行的操作施加严格边界：

  1. Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 与可验证的来源追溯（观察）：经由 AURA 的 Model Gateway 路由的每条提示词和补全输出，都会由 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 评估，以执行内容、主题和安全策略。知识库检索按组织隔离，每份 Brief 都必须包含经过验证的行内引用，注明分析了哪些时间窗口，以及哪些时段的传感器数据不可用。
  2. 网络隔离的只读沙箱与经人工批准的提议（提议）：Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Code Interpreter microVM 在 AWS 托管的隔离环境中运行，不具备通往工厂设备的网络路由、凭证或 API 路径。自动化 Routines 严格以只读模式运行。当工程师使用交互式会话提议更改设置时，平台要求操作员以企业身份明确进行人工批准，并在之后通过工厂遥测数据验证实际物理结果。
  3. 边缘端不可绕过的确定性第 1 层基础控制（边界约束与基础控制）：云端优化应用不会直接驱动现场硬件。它们在平台的基础控制层之上运行，在工程批准的范围内下发设定值计划。在工厂现场，边缘 Kubernetes 集群实时在本地运行下载的基础控制说明，执行确定性的状态机防护、变化率限制、运行边界和设备联锁；云服务、优化应用或 AI 智能体均无法绕过这些机制。
  4. 独立的物理硬件保护：在 ATLAS 软件定义控制器之下，工厂的物理机械和现场接线实施独立的硬接线保护层，包括安全继电器、本地可编程跳闸装置，以及机械泄压和过温保护装置。

成果与经验

CrossnoKaye 表示，在食品加工、工业制冷、骨料与采矿以及制造工厂中，将软件定义边缘控制、持续云端优化和 AURA 相结合，已将批次干燥时间的标准差降低了 34%（达到目标产出率规格的产品增加了 6%），并在采石场运营中识别出每年超过 50,000 吨的可挽回产量缺口。超过 5,000 个 AI 智能体监测着客户设施中的 10,000 多项工厂资产（整个 ATLAS 设施群中包含超过 13,000 台受控设备和设备单元）。过去需要花数小时导出历史数据库 CSV、交叉核对 PLC 梯形图逻辑并制作电子表格的调查，如今可在四分钟内完成，并在早班会议前通过 Amazon SES 交付附带引用的技术 Brief。

在多座工业设施中构建和运行 AURA 的过程中，有三点经验尤为突出：

  1. 添加 AI 之前，先统一工厂模型和控制逻辑：只有当智能体能够在一个一致的模型中读取工艺拓扑、已部署的基础控制说明和联锁、设置变更历史以及优化器状态，而不是拼接六个互不相连的工厂系统时，它才能诊断真实的物理根因，例如区分下游回料输送带打滑与二级破碎机故障。
  2. 在操作员的日常工作流中交付价值，而不是作为一个需要另外使用的工具：工厂团队忙于运行设备。如果 AI 助手是一个独立入口，工程师必须从空白提示词开始，日常采用就会停滞。将 AURA 嵌入每日班次节奏——由后台 Routines 在夜间捕捉异常，在 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 中运行 Python 分析，将附带引用的 Brief 发送至工程师邮箱，并支持一键转入已预载上下文的 Chat——意味着操作员能够在正常工作中看到价值，无需另外使用一个独立产品。
  3. 用代码而非提示词实施数据、覆盖范围和安全契约：在工厂中，缺失一小时的传感器数据，并不等于这一小时没有事件，而未经验证的计算可能将维护人员派到错误的机器旁。在工具契约中明确数据覆盖缺口，在提取二进制 Apache Parquet 输出前于 AgentCore 沙箱内验证 pandas.DataFrame 模式，并在边缘 Kubernetes 集群上实施确定性的基础控制边界，可以在概率性模型错误影响操作员或设备之前将其拦截。

结论

重工业中可靠的物理 AI，需要让模型以工厂真实的设备拓扑和控制逻辑为依据，并用可验证的 Python 计算支撑每项定量论断。结合 Amazon Bedrock Guardrails 和 Amazon Bedrock AgentCore 中的隔离 Python 沙箱，ATLAS 和 AURA 使智能体能够基于实时设施本体、基础控制说明、设置历史、物理 I/O、优化状态和合成读数进行推理，通过 Amazon SES 交付可核查的工程答案和附带引用的技术 Brief，同时将确定性的安全控制牢牢保留在工厂现场。
